---
type: pain_pattern
id: pp-upper-trapezius-tp1
title: Upper trapezius trigger point (TrP1)
structure: FMA:9626
kind: trigger_point
referral_regions: [FMA:32519, FMA:13710]
common_causes:
  - Sustained shoulder elevation (phone between ear and shoulder, high desk)
  - Carrying loads on one shoulder
  - Forward-head posture during screen work
aggravating:
  - Prolonged static neck postures
  - Cold draughts on the neck
  - Emotional stress and shoulder bracing
relieving:
  - Supported arms while seated
  - Heat to the upper shoulder
  - Gentle contralateral side-bending stretch
red_flags:
  - Neck pain after trauma
  - Pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, or night pain
  - Progressive arm weakness, numbness, or clumsiness
sources: [travell-simons-vol1]
---
The most common trigger point in the upper fibres of trapezius sits in the free
border of the muscle roughly midway between the acromion and the spinous process
of C7. Its referred pain classically climbs the posterolateral neck to the mastoid
region and can extend into the temple, presenting as a "tension-type" headache.
Patients often describe a heavy, aching shoulder that is worse at the end of a
working day.
